output.summary: KEP-2712 makes kubelet graceful node shutdown order and budget pods by priority value rather than only critical vs. regular, using configurable priority-range shutdown periods. Status is implementable at stage beta.
output.rationale: The existing graceful node shutdown only distinguished critical and regular pods, which gave little control over shutdown order. Kubernetes API conventions discourage hard-coding behavior by name, so the design uses priority class values instead. Maintainers discussed ranges with no pods being skipped immediately and bounded wait times that pod authors cannot control.

alternatives.option: Keep only critical vs. regular pod handling from KEP-2000
alternatives.why_not: The readme says there is a need for finer control over shutdown order beyond critical and regular pods.

alternatives.option: Look up pod priority class names to decide shutdown order
alternatives.why_not: The readme says kubernetes API design discourages hard coding anything by instances of name, so values are used instead.

evidence.quote: there is a need to allow more fine grained control over the pod shutdown order beyond _critical_ and _regular_ pods
Instead of looking at the pod priority class names, we can instead look at the pod priority class values to allow more control over pod shutdown order.
If we allocate 2 minutes for pods in a 1000 - 10000 range and there are no actual pods then we don't artificially wait for 2 minutes but move on to the next range.
Maybe add something along the lines of "If neither are specified, then Graceful Node Shutdown feature is disabled."
